The Straits are open to the Allies, the army is to go home and the garrisons in Arabia, Syria and Mesopotamia are to surrender. The war that the empire entered at the order of one minister and one German admiral ends with the empire's capital under Allied guns, and with a population that was told, for four years, that it was winning.▶ SHOW THE MAPConstantinopleDamascusAleppoNablusNazarethMudrosSettled recordThe German ships, August 1914: kept out of the Straits. Entering the war, 1914: the Black Sea raid, and war with Russia. Sarikamis, December 1914: the offensive in the snow. The Suez Canal, February 1915: the Fourth Army kept in Palestine. Gallipoli, April 1915: the divisions placed above the beaches. Kut, winter of 1915-16: the town stormed. Erzurum, 1916: the fortress held until it fell. The Hejaz, 1916: Medina held to the end of the war. The Yildirim, 1917: sent to Palestine. Jerusalem, 1917: the city left undefended. The Caucasus, 1918: the Army of Islam sent to Baku. Palestine, September 1918: the line held. What actually happened: the armistice of Mudros was signed on 30 October 1918 and took effect on 31 October. The Ottoman army and navy were demobilised
